meta.title: FreeCAD tool map for AI agents
meta.source: FreeCAD main branch, command IDs extracted from src/Mod/*
meta.read_me_first: Each tool has: id (GUI command for Gui.runCommand), py (scripted equivalent), after (what must exist first), next (what usually follows). Follow `after`/`next` to plan a sequence; use `py` to execute. Prefer py over GUI commands: GUI commands act on the current selection and active object, scripting does not.

fields.id: Gui.runCommand('<id>', 0) - needs correct selection + active workbench
fields.after: objects/state that must exist before this makes sense

conventions.imports: import FreeCAD as App, FreeCADGui as Gui, Part, Sketcher, Draft, Mesh, Import
conventions.recompute: doc.recompute() after every geometry change. Nothing updates without it. Check obj.State for 'Invalid'/'Touched'.
conventions.active_doc: doc = App.ActiveDocument or App.newDocument('Name'). App.setActiveDocument(doc.Name) also needed if GUI commands will run.
conventions.active_body: PartDesign features go into the ACTIVE body. Set it: Gui.ActiveDocument.ActiveView.setActiveObject('pdbody', body). Or skip GUI entirely and use body.newObject(...) which always targets that body.
conventions.workbench: Gui.activateWorkbench('PartDesignWorkbench') - only needed before Gui.runCommand. Names: PartDesignWorkbench, SketcherWorkbench, PartWorkbench, DraftWorkbench, AssemblyWorkbench, TechDrawWorkbench, FemWorkbench, SpreadsheetWorkbench, MeshWorkbench, CAMWorkbench, BIMWorkbench.
conventions.selection: Gui.Selection.clearSelection(); Gui.Selection.addSelection(doc.Name, obj.Name, 'Face3'). Subelement names are 1-indexed strings: Vertex1, Edge2, Face3.
conventions.units: All lengths are mm, angles degrees. Values accept plain floats or 'App.Units.Quantity("10 mm")'.
conventions.expressions: obj.setExpression('Length', 'Spreadsheet.width * 2') - drives a property from a formula. Clear with setExpression('Length', None).
conventions.undo: doc.openTransaction('name') ... doc.commitTransaction() / doc.abortTransaction(). Wrap multi-step edits so one undo reverts the whole operation.

gotchas: Topological naming: 'Face3' can point at a different face after any upstream edit. Attach sketches to datum planes or origin planes, not to faces, whenever the model will be parametric.
A PartDesign Body has exactly one solid. Two disconnected lumps = error. Use a Part Boolean or separate bodies instead.
First feature in a body must be additive (Pad/Revolution/AdditiveLoft/primitive). A Pocket first will fail.
Sketches used by Pad/Pocket must be closed and non-self-intersecting. Check sk.Shape.Wires and sk.solve()==0.

body.newObject() inserts the feature and makes it the tip IMMEDIATELY. Read body.Tip into a variable BEFORE creating a dress-up feature (Fillet/Chamfer/Draft/Thickness), or its Base points at itself and the feature silently does nothing - no exception, no error state, unchanged volume.
body.Tip is the last feature; body.Shape is the tip's shape. Insert features before the tip with PartDesign_MoveTip.
Mixing Part booleans and PartDesign features on the same object breaks the parametric chain. Pick one paradigm per body.
Objects are referenced by .Name (immutable, e.g. 'Pad001'), shown by .Label (user-editable, may duplicate). Always resolve by Name.
doc.removeObject(name) does not remove dependents; check obj.InList first.
Sketcher constraint indices: geometry is 0-based; PointPos is 1=start 2=end 3=center. The external/axis geometry uses negative indices (-1=X axis, -2=Y axis, -1,1=origin point).
Draft tools need a working plane: App.DraftWorkingPlane / Draft.setWorkingPlane, otherwise geometry lands on XY.

Document.note: Everything needs a document. Root of every tree.
Force with doc.recompute(None, True, True) when features are stuck Touched.
Check obj.InList (dependents) first or you orphan features.
App::Part is a container with its own Placement - the unit of assembly. Distinct from the Part workbench.
Lightweight instance. Use for repeated parts instead of copying.

PartDesign.note: One body = one contiguous solid. body.newObject(type,name) adds features to THIS body regardless of GUI active object - always prefer it.
Origin planes: doc.XY_Plane / XZ_Plane / YZ_Plane exist inside every body's Origin. MapMode 'FlatFace' on a plane/face, 'ObjectXY' on a datum.

PartDesign.py: pad = body.newObject('PartDesign::Pad','Pad'); pad.Profile = sk; pad.Length = 10; pad.Midplane = False; pad.Reversed = False
PartDesign.note: Type: 0=Length 1=UpToLast 2=UpToFirst 3=UpToFace 4=TwoLengths. UpToFace needs pad.UpToFace=(obj,['Face3']).
Subtractive. Same Type enum as Pad; Type=1 (ThroughAll) is the common one.

after: closed sketch, axis not crossing profile
PartDesign.note: ReferenceAxis choices: (sk,['V_Axis']), (sk,['H_Axis']), (sk,['Axis0']) for a construction line, or a datum line.
Subtractive revolve.

PartDesign.py: l = body.newObject('PartDesign::AdditiveLoft','Loft'); l.Profile = sk1; l.Sections = [sk2, sk3]; l.Ruled = False; l.Closed = False
PartDesign.note: Section order matters; mismatched vertex counts produce twists.
Sweep. Spine is (object, [edge names]) - listing all edges of the path is required.
Threads, springs. Mode: 0=pitch-height, 1=pitch-turns, 2=height-turns.
The clean way to cut a real thread.

PartDesign.py: h = body.newObject('PartDesign::Hole','Hole'); h.Profile = sk; h.Threaded=False; h.HoleCutType='None'; h.Diameter=6; h.Depth=20; h.DepthType='Dimension'
after: sketch of circles on a face
PartDesign.note: Use this, not Pocket, for fasteners: ThreadType='ISOMetricProfile', ThreadSize='M6', HoleCutType='Countersink'/'Counterbore', Tapered, DrillPoint. The sketch circles' diameters are ignored - only their centres are used.

Types: AdditiveBox, AdditiveCylinder, AdditiveSphere, AdditiveCone, AdditiveEllipsoid, AdditiveTorus, AdditivePrism, AdditiveWedge. Faster than sketch+pad for simple shapes; position via .AttachmentOffset.
Subtractive{Box,Cylinder,Sphere,Cone,Ellipsoid,Torus,Prism,Wedge}.

CAPTURE body.Tip BEFORE calling newObject - newObject makes the new feature the tip instantly, so f.Base=(body.Tip,...) self-references and the fillet silently does nothing (no error, volume unchanged). Same trap for Chamfer/Draft/Thickness. Select a Face to fillet all its edges. Fillet late - it is the most fragile feature under topological renaming.
Same capture-the-tip-first rule as PartDesign_Fillet. ChamferType: 0=equal 1=two distances 2=distance+angle.

PartDesign.py: base = body.Tip; d = body.newObject('PartDesign::Draft','Draft'); d.Base = (base, ['Face1']); d.Angle = 3; d.NeutralPlane = (base, ['Face6'])
PartDesign.note: Same capture-the-tip-first rule as PartDesign_Fillet. Mould release angles. Apply before fillets.

PartDesign.py: base = body.Tip; t = body.newObject('PartDesign::Thickness','Thickness'); t.Base = (base, ['Face6']); t.Value = 2; t.Reversed = True
PartDesign.note: Same capture-the-tip-first rule as PartDesign_Fillet. The listed faces are the ones removed (the opening).
Patterns features, not faces. Occurrences includes the original.
Bolt circles. Angle=360 with n occurrences spaces them evenly (no duplicate at 360).
Chains patterns (linear x polar) so they compound instead of stacking.
Only usable inside a MultiTransform.
THE fix for topological naming: sketch on a datum plane offset from an origin plane instead of on a model face.
Stable rotation axis.
Local coordinate system - the cleanest joint target in Assembly.
Copies external geometry into this body so you can reference it. Static copy.
Preferred over ShapeBinder: works across App::Part containers and stays linked.
Type: 0=Fuse 1=Cut 2=Common. Merges another body INTO this one and consumes it.
Parametric copy of a whole body.
Rewind history to insert a feature in the middle of the tree.

Sketcher_geometry.note: Standalone sketch (Part workflow). Inside PartDesign use PartDesign_NewSketch.
Only needed for GUI commands. Scripting never needs edit mode.
addGeometry returns the index used by every constraint. Second arg True = construction geometry.

Sketcher_geometry.py: [sk.addGeometry(Part.LineSegment(pts[i], pts[i+1]), False) for i in range(len(pts)-1)]
Sketcher_geometry.note: Then coincident-constrain each end to the next start, or the profile is not closed.

Sketcher_geometry.py: import SketcherGui; sk.addGeometry(Part.LineSegment(...)) x4 + 2 Horizontal + 2 Vertical + 4 Coincident
Sketcher_geometry.note: No single API call. Fastest correct rectangle in script: 4 lines, coincident-chain them, then Horizontal on 0 and 2, Vertical on 1 and 3.
Normal must be (0,0,1) - sketch geometry lives in the sketch's local XY.
Angles in RADIANS here, unlike everywhere else in FreeCAD.
Args: major-axis point, minor-axis point, centre.
Use Part.BSplineCurve().interpolate(pts) to pass THROUGH points instead of using them as poles.

Sketcher_geometry.py: bs = Part.BSplineCurve(); bs.buildFromPolesMultsKnots(poles, mults, knots, True)
Sketcher_geometry.note: Closed spline.
Construction points are excellent stable references.
Variants: Sketcher_CreateTriangle/Square/Pentagon/Hexagon/Heptagon/Octagon/RegularPolygon. Scripted: build n lines + a construction circle + Equal constraints.
Also Sketcher_CreateArcSlot, Sketcher_CreateOblong (rounded rectangle).

Sketcher_geometry.py: sk.fillet(geoId1, pos1, geoId2, pos2, radius, True)
Sketcher_geometry.note: Sketch-level fillet; cheaper than a solid fillet and immune to face renaming.
Merges into one B-spline.

Sketcher_geometry.py: sk.addRectangularArray(geoIdList, App.Vector(dx,dy,0), True, cols, rows, True)

Sketcher_geometry.note: Construction geometry is not exported to Pad/Pocket - use it for centrelines, bolt circles, symmetry axes.
External geometry gets NEGATIVE indices starting at -3 (-1 and -2 are the sketch axes). Fragile under topological renaming.
Copies geometry AND constraints from another sketch.
MapMode values: Deactivated, FlatFace, ObjectXY, ObjectXZ, ObjectYZ, TangentPlane, NormalToEdge, Concentric, ThreePointsPlane.

Sketcher_geometry.py: print(sk.solve(), sk.FullyConstrained, sk.Shape.isClosed() if sk.Shape.Wires else None)
Sketcher_geometry.note: ALWAYS run before padding. solve()==0 means solved. Also check sk.OpenVertices == [] for a closed profile.

Sketcher_constraints.note: PointPos: 1=start 2=end 3=centre. Axis refs: geoId -1 = X axis, -2 = Y axis; the origin point is (-1, 1). Add geometric constraints BEFORE dimensional ones - the solver converges far better.
The workhorse. Chain endpoints to close a profile. Coincident to (-1,1) pins geometry to the origin.
Endpoint-to-endpoint tangency (4 args) also enforces coincidence - do not add a separate Coincident or you get a redundancy.
Cheapest way to cut the DOF count on symmetric shapes.
Symmetric about the Y axis here. Better than two mirrored dimensions.
Freezes one element. Escape hatch for hard-to-constrain splines.
Adds DistanceX + DistanceY. Convenient but over-constrains easily - prefer explicit constraints.
Forms: (g1, len) line length; (g1,p1,g2,p2,len) point-to-point; (g1,p1,g2,len) point-to-line.
Use Diameter for holes - it matches how the part is manufactured and inspected.
Non-driving = a measurement readout instead of a rule. Useful for reporting a derived length.
THE way to parametrically drive a model. Name the constraint (sk.renameConstraint(i,'width')) then sk.setDatum('width', 25).
Diagnose under-constraint. Also: sk.ConflictingConstraints, sk.RedundantConstraints, sk.PartiallyRedundantConstraints, sk.MalformedConstraints - all should be empty lists.
Deleting shifts all higher indices down. Delete in descending order.

Part.note: Non-parametric-history CSG. Faster than PartDesign when you just need a shape; no feature tree to maintain.
Types: Part::Box, Cylinder, Sphere, Cone, Torus, Prism, Wedge, Helix, Spiral, Ellipsoid, Plane, Vertex, Line, RegularPolygon.

Part.py: c = doc.addObject('Part::Cut','Cut'); c.Base = a; c.Tool = b
Part.note: Base minus Tool. Both inputs get hidden and become children.
MultiFuse takes a list; Part::Fuse takes Base/Tool. Prefer MultiFuse.
Direct TopoShape ops (cut/fuse/common/section) skip the document entirely - fastest path for throwaway geometry. Part.show(shape,'Name') puts it in the document.

Part.py: e = doc.addObject('Part::Extrusion','Extrude'); e.Base = sk; e.DirMode='Normal'; e.LengthFwd=10; e.Solid=True
Part.note: Set Solid=True or you get a hollow shell.

Part.py: s = doc.addObject('Part::Sweep','Sweep'); s.Sections=[profile]; s.Spine=(path,['Edge1']); s.Solid=True; s.Frenet=True

Part.note: Edges is a list of (1-based edge index, start radius, end radius).

Part.py: o = doc.addObject('Part::Offset','Offset'); o.Source=obj; o.Value=2; o.Mode=0; o.Join=0
Part.note: Join: 0=Arc 1=Tangent 2=Intersection. Part_Offset2D for planar wires.
Negative value = inward.
transformGeometry is the only true non-uniform scale; Placement cannot scale.
obj.Shape.slices(dir, [z1,z2,...]) for a whole stack - the basis of any slicer.
View-only cutaway. Does not modify geometry.
Check shell.isClosed() first or the solid is invalid.
Removes the co-planar seam faces booleans leave behind. Do this before exporting or filleting - it usually fixes 'fillet failed'.
First thing to run when a downstream operation fails.
Removes selected faces (holes, fillets) from a dumb import.
Flips normals. Fixes inside-out imported meshes/shells.
Breaks the parametric link - the way to freeze a result.
STL to B-rep. Produces a faceted shell, not smooth surfaces. Follow with Part.Solid() then refine.
Assemble shapes bottom-up from selected sub-elements.
STEP/IGES/BREP. Import.export([obj], '/path/out.step').
Part::JoinConnect / JoinEmbed / JoinCutout - for joining pipes and sheet-like bodies.
Splits everything at every intersection. Also makeSlice, makeXOR.

Part.py: d = obj.Shape.distToShape(other.Shape)[0]; obj.Shape.Volume; obj.Shape.Area; obj.Shape.BoundBox; obj.Shape.CenterOfMass
Part.note: Everything the Measure workbench does is available directly on Shape. Also Shape.getMomentOfInertia / .Inertia via Shape.MatrixOfInertia.

Draft.note: Do this FIRST. Every Draft tool draws on the working plane; wrong plane is the #1 Draft failure.
closed=True + face=True gives an extrudable face in one call - the quickest 2D-to-3D route in all of FreeCAD.
An arc is a Draft circle with start/end angles. Draft_Arc_3Points: Draft.make_arc_3points([p1,p2,p3]).
The only way to get engravable/embossable text geometry. Needs a real font file path.
copy=True duplicates. Works on any object, not just Draft ones.
Edges to wire, closed wire to face, faces to shell to solid. Run it repeatedly; it climbs one level each time. Draft_Downgrade goes the other way.
The bridge from Draft into a constrainable PartDesign workflow.
Chain links, fence posts, anything following a curve.
Parametric copy that tracks the original and can be scaled.
Flattens 3D to 2D lines - the route from a model to a DXF.
Layers map to DXF/DWG layers on export.
GUI-only. Irrelevant to scripted work; snapping does not apply to API calls.

Assembly.note: An assembly is an App::Part subclass; it auto-creates a JointGroup, ViewGroup, etc. Nested assemblies are allowed.

Assembly.py: lnk = asm.newObject('App::Link','Link'); lnk.LinkedObject = part_obj; lnk.Placement = App.Placement(...)
Assembly.note: Components are App::Links, never copies. Insert the same part N times = N links, one definition.
Top-down design: model the part in place inside the assembly.

Assembly.py: g = asm.newObject('Assembly::JointGroup'...)  # GUI command is far simpler here
Assembly.note: GROUND EXACTLY ONE COMPONENT FIRST. An ungrounded assembly has no datum and the solver drifts. This is the single most common assembly mistake.

Assembly.py: jg = asm.Proxy.getJointGroup(asm) if hasattr(asm,'Proxy') else doc.getObject('Joints'); j = jg.newObject('App::FeaturePython','Fixed'); # then JointObject.Joint(j, 0)
Assembly.note: Scripting joints is awkward - the practical route is Gui.Selection.addSelection() on two features then Gui.runCommand('Assembly_CreateJointFixed',0). Once created, set j.JointType, j.Reference1, j.Reference2, j.Distance, j.Angle.
1 rotational DOF. Reference a circular edge or an LCS on each part; FreeCAD derives the axis.
Rotate + slide on the same axis. Shafts in bores.
Also does plane-plane offset, tangency, and point-on-line depending on what you reference.
Motion coupling only, not geometry. Also 'RackPinion', 'Screw', 'Belt'.
asm.solve() returns 0 on success. asm.isPartConnected(obj), asm.undoSolve() also exist.
Diagnostic: which parts are still free. Companions: SelectConflictingConstraints, SelectRedundantConstraints, SelectMalformedConstraints.
Bill of materials as a Spreadsheet - place it on a TechDraw page.
Kinematic motion study driven by the Ondsel solver.
Debug dump of the solver model.

TechDraw.note: Root of every drawing. Templates live in <resource>/Mod/TechDraw/Templates/.

TechDraw.py: v = doc.addObject('TechDraw::DrawViewPart','View'); v.Source = [body]; v.Direction = App.Vector(0,0,1); v.XDirection = App.Vector(1,0,0); v.Scale = 1; page.addView(v); v.X = 100; v.Y = 150
TechDraw.note: Direction is the view direction. X/Y position on the page in mm. Set v.HardHidden/v.SmoothVisible for line style. Always doc.recompute() - views render lazily.

TechDraw.py: g = doc.addObject('TechDraw::DrawProjGroup','ProjGroup'); page.addView(g); g.Source=[body]; g.ProjectionType='Third Angle'; g.addProjection('Front'); g.addProjection('Top'); g.addProjection('Right')
TechDraw.note: The right way to make a standard multi-view drawing. Anchor is 'Front'; the others align automatically.

TechDraw.py: s = doc.addObject('TechDraw::DrawViewSection','Section'); s.BaseView = v; s.SectionNormal = App.Vector(0,-1,0); s.SectionOrigin = App.Vector(0,0,0); page.addView(s)
TechDraw.note: TechDraw_ComplexSection for stepped/aligned sections through a sketch path.

TechDraw.py: d = doc.addObject('TechDraw::DrawViewDetail','Detail'); d.BaseView = v; d.AnchorPoint=App.Vector(10,10,0); d.Radius=5; d.Scale=4

TechDraw.note: Snapshot of the current 3D viewport, including colours - the quick way to get an isometric picture onto a sheet.
Type: Distance, DistanceX, DistanceY, Radius, Diameter, Angle, Angle3Pt, Area. TechDraw sub-element names are 0-INDEXED (Edge0), unlike the 3D model's 1-indexed names.
Smart dimension - infers the type from the selection. The one to use interactively.

TechDraw.py: a = doc.addObject('TechDraw::DrawViewAnnotation','Note'); a.Text=['NOTES:','1. Deburr all edges.']; page.addView(a)

TechDraw.note: TechDraw_GeometricHatch for standards-based patterns from a .pat file.
Also TechDraw_WeldSymbol on a leader line.

TechDraw.py: sv = doc.addObject('TechDraw::DrawViewSpreadsheet','Sheet'); sv.Source = sheet; sv.CellStart='A1'; sv.CellEnd='C10'; page.addView(sv)
TechDraw.note: Puts a BOM or parts table on the drawing.
exportPageAsDxf(page, path) for CAD interchange. PDF: use the GUI print dialog or FreeCADGui print-to-file.
Pages default to not auto-updating on big models. Set KeepUpdated when scripting or your views stay blank.

Spreadsheet.note: The parameter table. Drive the whole model from here.
Values are always strings. Formulas start with '=': sheet.set('B3','=B1*2').
Aliases are what make a cell referenceable. Without one the cell is invisible to the model.
Reference named sketch constraints as Constraints.<name>. This is the whole point of parametric CAD - one table drives every dimension.
get() returns the evaluated value, getContents() the raw string.
Cells carry units. A unitless cell driving a Length property works, but mixing units in a formula silently fails - keep the sheet consistent.

FEM.note: Every FEM object is created by an ObjectsFem.makeX(doc, name) factory, then added: analysis.addObject(obj). The order below IS the required order - skipping a step gives a silent empty result.
Container for the whole study. setActiveAnalysis is required before any GUI FEM command.
AnalysisType: static, frequency, thermomech, buckling, check. Alternatives: makeSolverElmer (multiphysics/EM/CFD), makeSolverZ88, makeSolverMystran.

FEM.py: mat = ObjectsFem.makeMaterialSolid(doc,'Material'); analysis.addObject(mat); m = mat.Material; m['Name']='Steel'; m['YoungsModulus']='210000 MPa'; m['PoissonRatio']='0.30'; m['Density']='7900 kg/m^3'; mat.Material = m
FEM.note: mat.Material is a dict that must be reassigned wholesale - editing in place does nothing. Values are unit strings. Leave References empty to apply to everything.
CFD only. Also makeMaterialMechanicalNonlinear (plasticity), makeMaterialReinforced (concrete).
At least one fixed (or displacement) constraint is mandatory - without it the model is unrestrained and the solve diverges.
Prescribed motion, or partial restraint (symmetry planes).

FEM.py: f = ObjectsFem.makeConstraintForce(doc,'Force'); analysis.addObject(f); f.References=[(body,'Face2')]; f.Force='100 N'; f.Reversed=False
FEM.note: Total force spread over the referenced faces, not per-face.
Needs Density set on the material.
Rotating parts - flywheels, impellers.
Expensive and fragile. Use makeConstraintTie for bonded (glued) interfaces instead - far more robust.
Thermal chain: makeConstraintTemperature, makeConstraintHeatflux, makeConstraintBodyHeatSource, makeConstraintInitialTemperature.
Elastic foundation. Also makeConstraintRigidBody, makeConstraintTransform (cylindrical/local coords), makeConstraintPlaneRotation, makeConstraintSectionPrint.
Shell thickness for 2D meshes. makeElementGeometry1D for beam cross-sections, makeElementRotation1D for beam orientation, makeElementFluid1D for pipe networks.

FEM.py: mesh = ObjectsFem.makeMeshGmsh(doc,'Mesh'); mesh.Shape = body; mesh.CharacteristicLengthMax='5 mm'; mesh.ElementOrder='2nd'; analysis.addObject(mesh); import femmesh.gmshtools as gt; gt.GmshTools(mesh).create_mesh()
FEM.note: Requires gmsh on PATH. create_mesh() returns an error string ('' = success). ElementOrder '2nd' is almost always what you want for stress accuracy. Check mesh.FemMesh.NodeCount > 0 before solving.
Built-in, no external binary. Less control than gmsh.
Local refinement at stress concentrations. Also makeMeshBoundaryLayer (CFD), makeMeshTransfiniteVolume (structured).
Named node/element sets exported to the solver deck.

FEM.py: from femtools import ccxtools; fea = ccxtools.FemToolsCcx(analysis, solver); fea.update_objects(); fea.setup_working_dir(); fea.check_prerequisites(); fea.write_inp_file(); fea.ccx_run(); fea.load_results()
FEM.note: check_prerequisites() returns a message string - if non-empty, STOP and report it; it names exactly what is missing. This is the best diagnostic in the whole FEM module.

FEM.py: res = [o for o in analysis.Group if o.isDerivedFrom('Fem::FemResultObject')][0]; print(max(res.vonMises), max(res.DisplacementLengths))
FEM.note: Result fields: vonMises, DisplacementVectors, DisplacementLengths, MaxShear, PrincipalMax/Med/Min, Temperature, ReinforcementRatio. Compare max(vonMises) to the material yield to answer 'will it hold'.
Post-processing pipeline; filters attach to it: makePostVtkFilterClipRegion, ClipScalar, CutFunction, Warp, Contours, makePostFilterGlyph.
Data along a line. Also makePostHistogram, makePostTable for numeric extraction.
Clear before re-running or old results are silently kept.
Working reference models for every analysis type - the fastest way to learn a correct setup.

Mesh_and_IO.note: Works directly on a solid - it tessellates automatically. For print quality set the tessellation first via a Mesh_FromPartShape.

Mesh_and_IO.py: m = doc.addObject('Mesh::Feature','Mesh'); m.Mesh = MeshPart.meshFromShape(Shape=body.Shape, LinearDeflection=0.1, AngularDeflection=0.5, Relative=False)
Mesh_and_IO.note: import MeshPart. LinearDeflection controls print fidelity - 0.01-0.1 mm for FDM. This is the correct STL export path.
Run before exporting for print. m.Mesh.removeNonManifolds(), .removeDuplicatedFacets(), .fixIndices(), .harmonizeNormals() are the repair calls.
Mesh booleans are far more forgiving than B-rep booleans on messy scan data.
STEP is the interchange format that preserves solids. Set import prefs via ParamGet('User parameter:BaseApp/Preferences/Mod/Import').
Imports as Draft objects. Upgrade then Draft2Sketch to make it parametric.
Logo-to-3D pipeline: import SVG, Draft.upgrade to faces, Part::Extrusion.
Shape-level exporters skip the document layer - the fastest programmatic export.

Material_Measure_Misc.py: obj.ShapeMaterial = <material>  # GUI: Material workbench, or set ViewObject.ShapeAppearance
Material_Measure_Misc.note: Assigning a material gives correct Density for mass calculations and drives FEM/BIM takeoffs.

Material_Measure_Misc.py: v = obj.Shape.Volume; mass = v * density_kg_per_mm3; c = obj.Shape.CenterOfMass
Material_Measure_Misc.note: Volume is mm^3. Steel ~7.9e-6 kg/mm^3. CenterOfMass and MatrixOfInertia answer most engineering questions without a workbench.
Instant 'will it fit in the printer' check.
THE way for an AI to see its own work. Take a screenshot after every significant step and check it.
How to learn what the user is pointing at. getCompleteSelection() includes sub-elements across documents.

Material_Measure_Misc.py: obj.OutList  # what it depends on;  obj.InList  # what depends on it
Material_Measure_Misc.note: Traverse the model programmatically. doc.Objects, doc.getObject(name), doc.getObjectsByLabel(label).
Persisting generated scripts. Macro dir: App.getUserMacroDir(True).
All settings are here. Read before writing; changes are immediate and persistent.

Material_Measure_Misc.py: Gui.activateWorkbench('CAMWorkbench')  # then CAM_Job, CAM_Profile, CAM_Pocket, CAM_Drilling, CAM_PostProcess
Material_Measure_Misc.note: Chain: Job (pick model + stock + tool table) -> ToolBitLibrary -> operations (Profile/Pocket/Adaptive/Drilling/Surface) -> Simulator -> PostProcess to G-code.

Material_Measure_Misc.py: import Arch; Arch.makeWall(baseline, length=5000, width=200, height=3000)
Material_Measure_Misc.note: Arch/BIM chain: makeSite -> makeBuilding -> makeFloor -> makeWall/makeStructure -> makeWindow (needs a wall host) -> makeSectionPlane -> TechDraw. Arch.makeIfcProject for IFC export.
Surface workbench: Filling, GeomFillSurface, Sections, Curve on mesh, Blend curve. For organic shapes B-rep primitives cannot make.
Point clouds; ReverseEngineering workbench fits surfaces to them.

Parameters_VarSet.note: The one place to put parametric variables that drive dimensions. FreeCAD 1.0+. The OBJECT type is 'App::VarSet'. 'App::PropertyLength', 'App::PropertyLink' and friends are PROPERTY types - passing one to addObject fails with "is not a document object type".
addProperty(type, name, group, doc). Property type here, object type in addObject. Use PropertyLength for anything in mm so units follow.

How a parametric variable actually drives a dimension. This is the point of a VarSet: change vs.Bore, recompute, and every expression bound to it follows. Name the sketch constraint first, or there is nothing to bind to.
Drives every dependent feature. Prefer this over editing each feature.

flow_tree.note: Read '>' as 'is normally followed by'. Branches in [] are alternatives. This is the spine an agent should plan against.
flow_tree.root: Std_New > { PartDesign | Part | Draft | Assembly | Spreadsheet }
mechanical_part: > Sketcher geometry > Sketcher geometric constraints > Sketcher dimensional constraints > Sketcher_ValidateSketch
> PartDesign_NewSketch(on a face or a PartDesign_Plane) > PartDesign_Pocket [ | PartDesign_Hole | PartDesign_Groove ]
> Std_Save > { TechDraw_PageDefault | Mesh_FromPartShape | Import_STEP export | Assembly_Insert }

predecessor_index.note: Inverse lookup: 'to run X, you first need Y'. Answers 'why did this command grey out / fail'.
predecessor_index.PartDesign_Pad / Pocket / Revolution / G: a closed, non-self-intersecting sketch (or a face)
predecessor_index.PartDesign_Pocket / any subtractive: an existing solid in the body (the first feature must be additive)
predecessor_index.PartDesign_Fillet / Chamfer / Draft / Th: a solid, and specific Edge/Face names that survive recompute
predecessor_index.PartDesign_LinearPattern / PolarPattern: at least one feature to transform
predecessor_index.PartDesign_Hole: a sketch containing circles, positioned on a face
predecessor_index.Sketcher constraints: geometry already added, referenced by its returned index
predecessor_index.Sketcher_Projection (external geometry): the sketch attached to something near the target geometry
predecessor_index.Part booleans: two shapes that actually overlap (or the result is empty, not an error)
predecessor_index.TechDraw dimensions: a view that has actually rendered (KeepUpdated + recompute)
predecessor_index.FEM_SolverRun: mesh + material + at least one fixed constraint + at least one load
predecessor_index.Mesh_Export at print quality: an explicit Mesh_FromPartShape with a chosen deflection

failure_playbook.Pad failed / no solid: sk.solve()!=0, or the profile is open or self-intersecting. Check sk.OpenVertices and sk.Shape.Wires.
failure_playbook.'Result has multiple solids': The sketch has disjoint regions, or the feature does not touch the existing body. Split into separate bodies + Part_Fuse.
failure_playbook.Fillet/Chamfer fails: Part_RefineShape the input; reduce the radius below the smallest adjacent feature; apply fillets earlier in the tree.
failure_playbook.Feature moved to the wrong place after a: Topological naming. Replace face references with a PartDesign_Plane datum and re-attach the sketch.
failure_playbook.Sketch is over-constrained: Check sk.RedundantConstraints / ConflictingConstraints / PartiallyRedundantConstraints; delete in DESCENDING index order.
failure_playbook.Sketch will not fully constrain: sk.FullyConstrained is False - find the free DOF with Sketcher_SelectElementsWithDoFs; usually the profile is not pinned to the origin.
failure_playbook.Boolean produced nothing: The shapes do not overlap. Check obj.Shape.BoundBox and Placement.
failure_playbook.Imported STEP is one dumb solid: Expected. Use PartDesign_SubShapeBinder to reference it, or Part_Defeaturing to strip features.
failure_playbook.TechDraw dimension attaches to the wrong: TechDraw sub-elements are 0-indexed (Edge0), the 3D model's are 1-indexed (Edge1).
failure_playbook.Assembly parts fly apart: Nothing is grounded, or a joint is over-constrained. Ground one part, then add joints one at a time and solve after each.
failure_playbook.FEM solve produced no result: fea.check_prerequisites() - it names the missing piece. Usually no fixed constraint or an empty mesh (mesh.FemMesh.NodeCount == 0).
failure_playbook.FEM results look absurd: Units. YoungsModulus in MPa with force in N and length in mm is the consistent set.
failure_playbook.GUI command did nothing: Wrong workbench, or the selection/active object was not what the command expects. Prefer the 'py' form.
failure_playbook.Fillet/Chamfer ran with no error but not: Base is self-referencing: body.Tip was read after newObject() created the feature. Capture the tip first.
failure_playbook.'X' is not a document object type: A property type was passed to addObject. Objects are App::VarSet, PartDesign::Body, Spreadsheet::Sheet; App::PropertyLength / App::PropertyLink are properties and belong in obj.addProperty(...).
failure_playbook.parametric dimensions / one place to edi: App::VarSet (1.0+) or a Spreadsheet. VarSet_Create -> VarSet_AddProperty -> setExpression on the feature or on Constraints.<name>.

agent_playbook: Plan the whole feature tree before creating anything. Rework is expensive because features depend on names.
Use the 'py' column, not Gui.runCommand, wherever both exist. Scripted calls are deterministic; GUI commands depend on hidden selection state.
One doc.openTransaction / commitTransaction per logical step, so a bad step is one undo away.
recompute + check State after every feature, not at the end. Find the failing feature immediately.
Sketch on origin planes and datum planes. Only reference model faces when the model is finished and will not change.
Name things: obj.Label = 'MountingHole'. Name sketch constraints. A readable tree is a maintainable tree.
Constrain geometrically first (coincident, horizontal, tangent, equal, symmetric), dimension last. Fewer dimensions = a more robust sketch.
Put every driving number in a Spreadsheet with aliases from the start. Retrofitting expressions is tedious.
Verify visually: Gui.activeDocument().activeView().saveImage(path, 1920, 1080, 'White') and look at it.
Verify numerically: Shape.isValid(), len(Shape.Solids)==1, Shape.Volume, Shape.BoundBox against the intent.
Dress-up features (fillet, chamfer, draft, thickness) go last in the tree and are the first thing to remove when a rebuild breaks.
